title: Save Your Laptop
topicTitle: Contain an attack in the right order
topicBrief: Malware can run quietly in the background to steal data, create a backdoor, or damage files. Incident responders first identify the malicious process, cut its network access, and contain the damaged data. This is a fully scripted training simulation - no real process, file, or connection is touched.
scenario: Critical Alert: Unauthorized system modifications detected. A fictional payload is active on this laptop. Use the available response tools to stop it before the integrity meter falls further.

stages.title: Process Analyzer
stages.instruction: Step 1: Open the Process Analyzer and terminate the rogue application.
stages.hint1: Look for a process without a verified publisher before deciding it is malicious.
stages.hint2: The rogue process is consuming more than 80% of the CPU and has no verified signature.

items.name: sys_update_agent.exe
items.detail: Spawned from a temporary folder and repeatedly changes its process name.

items.name: cloud-backup.exe
items.detail: A scheduled backup is compressing files. High activity is expected during its daily window.

items.name: endpoint-protection.exe
items.detail: The antivirus scan is checking the Downloads folder after the alert.

stages.title: Network Firewall
stages.instruction: Step 2: The malware opened a backdoor. Open the Network Firewall to block its communication.
stages.hint1: Prioritise an unusual destination or port that is sending a large amount of data outward.
stages.hint2: The backdoor uses port 8088 and has sent far more data than the normal connections.

items.name: sys_update_agent.exe -> 198.51.100.77:8088
items.detail: The unverified process is sending a large, persistent outbound stream over an unusual port.

items.name: system-service -> updates.training.thm:443
items.detail: Encrypted HTTPS telemetry is expected for the simulated operating system.

items.name: cloud-backup.exe -> vault.training.thm:443
items.detail: The scheduled backup is using its normal verified cloud destination.

items.name: resolver -> dns.training.thm:53
items.detail: Normal DNS lookups for the laptop.

stages.title: File Quarantine
stages.instruction: Step 3: Secure compromised data. Open File Quarantine.
stages.hint1: A safe response preserves evidence and restores trusted copies instead of destroying everything.
stages.hint2: Choose the action that quarantines the payload and restores files from a known-good backup.

items.name: Quarantine malicious payload & restore from backup
items.metadata: Preserve evidence and recover trusted copies
items.detail: Isolates the payload for investigation and restores staged documents from the verified backup.

items.name: Delete files entirely
items.detail: Deleting user files destroys recoverable data and evidence; it is not the first remediation step.

items.name: Ignore warnings
items.detail: The malware could continue encrypting or exfiltrating files if warnings are ignored.

learn.title: EDR is an orderly response
learn.body: Endpoint Detection and Response is not about clicking the most alarming item. Identify the malicious process, isolate its communication, and preserve and restore data from trusted backups. Verified publishers and normal context help prevent damage to legitimate software.
